gbm_population_evidence.quote: WHO Grade 3 Glioma; WHO Grade 4 Glioma
History of World Health Organization (WHO) grade III or IV infiltrating glioma previously treated with first-line chemoradiotherapy.

gbm_population_flag.reason: Glioblastoma not named literally; included only via the D27C rule that grade 4/IV glioma without IDH requirement is historical glioblastoma, alongside grade III glioma.

candidate_evidence.quote: [EXPERIMENTAL] Diagnostic (Ga-68 PSMA-11, PET/CT): Patients receive Ga-68 PSMA-11 IV and then undergo PET/CT over 1 hour, 50-100 minutes after injection.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: MRI findings compatible with contrast-enhancing recurrent infiltrating glioma.

role_evidence.quote: This clinical trial evaluates whether gallium-68 (Ga-68) prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-11 positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography (CT) imaging is useful in differentiating between disease that has come back after a period of improvement (recurrence)

agents.drug_class_hint: 68Ga-labelled PSMA PET imaging tracer (gallium Ga 68 gozetotide)

source_quote.quote: To perform a radiology-pathology correlation of PSMA uptake at PET with tumor PSMA immunohistochemistry (IHC) immunostaining, tumor pathology features, and signal and enhancement characteristics at magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)

coder_notes: Diagnostic imaging trial: Ga-68 PSMA-11 (gozetotide) PET/CT to distinguish recurrence from treatment effect; no therapeutic agent, so no candidate. Population is WHO grade III or IV glioma with no IDH requirement; grade IV glioma treated as historical glioblastoma per D27C, hence mixed_glioma_gbm_named and historical terminology.
